title: Where the Zscaler MCP server's argument converters drop or choose silently: ZPA policy conditions and ZTW country names

prose.text: The MCP server converts some caller input before it reaches the SDK. Three converters at the pinned release return a well-formed result while discarding or choosing part of the input, and each has an open upstream issue.
{{v2-dict-branch-drops-flat-operands}} {{v1-to-v2-drops-v2-operands}} Whether the maintainers consider these defects, and whether a fix is planned, is not stated {{gap:converter-fix-status}}.
{{country-fuzzy-first-match}} Whether the helper rejects ambiguous input in a later release is open {{gap:country-ambiguity-fix}}.

v2-dict-branch-drops-flat-operands.statement: At the pinned release `convert_v2_to_sdk_format` enters its dict branch when every element is a dict, but reads only `cond.get("operands", [])` from each; a list of flat operand dicts with no `operands` key therefore yields an empty list with no error. Issue #109 reports that a policy rule can then be created or updated with none of the conditions the caller supplied, and was open when captured.

quotes: if isinstance(conditions, list) and all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in conditions):
operands = cond.get("operands", [])
raise ValueError(f"Unsupported conditions format: {type(conditions)}")
`convert_v2_to_sdk_format` returns an empty list for a list of operand dicts
So a caller passing operand dicts *without* an `{"operator", "operands"}` wrapper gets `[]` back with no error.
A policy-rule create or update that receives it therefore proceeds with an empty condition set

v1-to-v2-drops-v2-operands.statement: At the pinned release `convert_v1_to_v2_response` reads only an operand's `rhs` or `lhs`, and only for object types listed in `_V1_TO_V2_VALUE_TYPES` or `_V1_TO_V2_ENTRY_TYPES`, and skips a condition that ends with no operands. Issue #110 reports that operands already in v2 shape (`values` or `entry_values`) and operands of unlisted types are dropped with no error, so a read-convert-update flow strips them before the write; it was open when captured.

quotes: if obj_type in _V1_TO_V2_VALUE_TYPES:
elif obj_type in _V1_TO_V2_ENTRY_TYPES:
values_by_type[obj_type].append(str(rhs))
entries_by_type[obj_type].append({"lhs": str(lhs), "rhs": str(rhs)})
if not new_operands:
convert_v1_to_v2_response drops existing v2 operands and silently omits unlisted object types
When given operands that are already in v2 format (`values` or `entry_values`), it extracts nothing and returns `[]`.
Operands whose object type is not in `_V1_TO_V2_VALUE_TYPES` or `_V1_TO_V2_ENTRY_TYPES` are also silently dropped, with no error or warning.
existing v2 operands or unlisted criteria are stripped before the write is submitted.

country-fuzzy-first-match.statement: `validate_and_convert_country_code` tries `alpha_2`, `alpha_3`, `name`, `common_name` and `official_name` lookups and then `pycountry.countries.search_fuzzy`, and on the fuzzy path returns the first candidate without checking how many matched. Issue #108 reports that `Korea` resolves to `COUNTRY_KP` although `KR` also matches, with no error or warning, and was open when captured.

quotes: for getter in ("alpha_2", "alpha_3", "name", "common_name", "official_name"):
countries = pycountry.countries.search_fuzzy(country_input)
return f"COUNTRY_{countries[0].alpha_2}"
`validate_and_convert_country_code()` resolves its input through a chain of exact `pycountry` getters
The clearest case is the word `Korea`, which matches both `KP` and `KR` and resolves to `KP`.
'Korea' -> COUNTRY_KP

converter-fix-status.title: Whether the ZPA condition converters will be fixed
converter-fix-status.detail: Issues #109 and #110 were open with no maintainer reply when captured. Whether a release preserves flat operands, v2 operands and unlisted object types, or raises instead, is not stated. Check the changelog after 0.15.4 before relying on a read-convert-update flow for policy rules.
converter-fix-status.blocks: relying on an MCP policy-rule update to keep every condition the caller read

quotes: In read-convert-update flows, where a caller reads a rule via `zpa_get_access_policy_rule` and passes the returned `conditions` into `zpa_update_access_policy_rule`

country-ambiguity-fix.title: Whether the ZTW country helper will reject ambiguous names
country-ambiguity-fix.detail: Issue #108 was open with no maintainer reply when captured. Until a release changes it, a partial or ambiguous country name can persist as an unintended country; an alpha-2 code avoids the fuzzy path.
country-ambiguity-fix.blocks: passing free-text country names to ZTW destination-group tools

quotes: An input that matches more than one country is rejected with an error naming the alternatives
